title: Bug:
body:
Title: Consider built-in routing support in React core

React is an amazing library and has become the backbone of modern web applications.

One common requirement in almost every React web app is routing. Currently, developers must rely on third-party libraries such as react-router-dom. While these libraries are excellent, routing is such a fundamental need that it might be worth considering some level of built-in routing support in React itself.

Having an official, minimal router maintained alongside React could:
	•	Reduce dependency on third-party packages
	•	Improve beginner experience
	•	Ensure tighter integration with React features and future updates

Thank you for building such an awesome ecosystem and for continuously improving React.

title: Bug: <Activity /> does not behave as described in the official documentation.
body:
React version: 
v19.2.0

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Render `<Activity>Hello, World!</Activity>`
 ```jsx
   <Activity>
     Hello, World!
   </Activity>
```

2. Render `<Activity><ComponentThatJustReturnsText /></Activity>`
```jsx
const ComponentThatJustReturnsText = () => "Hello, World!";

<Activity>
  <ComponentThatJustReturnsText />
</Activity>
```

3. Regardless of whether the mode prop is provided or not, both plain text and components that return only text are rendered in the DOM.


Link to code example:
Reproducible with a minimal example using only React (no additional dependencies).

## The current behavior
Text-only children inside `<Activity />` are rendered correctly in the DOM.
- Passing a plain string (`"Hello, World!"`) directly works as expected.
- Passing a component that returns only a string also renders without issues.
- The `mode` prop still behaves correctly, and visibility changes are applied as expected.

## The expected behavior
### According to the official documentation:

> An Activity that just renders text will not render anything rather than rendering hidden text, 
because there’s no corresponding DOM element to apply visibility changes to. 
For example, <Activity mode="hidden"><ComponentThatJustReturnsText /></Activity> will not produce any output in the DOM for const ComponentThatJustReturnsText = () => "Hello, World!";.

_Based on this description, text-only children should not produce any DOM output. However, in practice, they are rendered normally._


## Related link

React documentation:
https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#caveats

title: [react-compiler-healthcheck] Add --verbose to list components that failed compilation
body:
### What kind of issue is this?

- [ ] React Compiler core (the JS output is incorrect, or your app works incorrectly after optimization)
- [ ] babel-plugin-react-compiler (build issue installing or using the Babel plugin)
- [ ] eslint-plugin-react-hooks (build issue installing or using the eslint plugin)
- [x] react-compiler-healthcheck (build issue installing or using the healthcheck script)

### Link to repro

N/A — feature request.

### Repro steps

Healthcheck only prints "Successfully compiled X out of Y components" and does not show which components failed.

**Proposal:** Add a `--verbose` flag to print for each failed component:
- file path
- location (line/column when available)
- error reason

The data is already collected in `ActionableFailures` / `OtherFailures` in `reactCompiler.ts`; it only needs to be printed when the flag is set. That would make it possible to fix remaining violations and to trust the reported counts.

**Related:** #29078 (closed), #29677 (open — "how do I find the remaining components?").

### How often does this bug happen?

Every time

### What version of React are you using?

19.2.4

### What version of React Compiler are you using?

babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0 (via Expo SDK 54); react-compiler-healthcheck@19.1.0-rc.3

title: [DevTools Bug]: confused on prerender pages and resulting in high-cpu usage loop
body:
### Website or app

example; https://yuri.twintail.org/chrome/prerendering/specrules.html

### Repro steps

Hello, I'm Takashi from Google Chrome team.

I've investigated high-cpu usage issue on prerendering, and noticed that the React Developer Tools seems to be a root cause.
The original report for the chromium project is here; https://crbug.com/478909972

Steps:
1. Install React Developer Tools Extension (from the Chrome Web Store)
2. Visit a page that uses specupationrules
3. Open Chrome's Task manager from ... > More tools >, and see CPU usages
4. Usage for the prerender pages shows higher CPU usages
5. Open DevTools
6. Prerender pages' CPU usages get much higher, and frame of the React Developer Tools spends almost 100%

This needs that the current page is accessible from the Extensions. e.g., they would not have a permission to touch the New Tab Page, and this doesn't happen there.

Also, this happens with Chrome UI triggered pretenders too. So, even if the page doesn't use the speculationrules, the problem could happen when users type something in the Omnibox, and Chrome has confidence on the next navigating page.

I suspect this is because the extension doesn't expect the Chrome's recent MPArch: Multi-Page Architecture, and is confused on multiple page navigations.
Here is a resource for the prerender and link for its impact on the Extension system.
[Prerender pages in Chrome for instant page navigations > Impact on extensions
](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/prerender-pages#impact_on_extensions)

title: [Fizz] Bug: Nested suspense boundary with suspended fallback: "A previously unvisited boundary must have exactly one root segment"
body:
There's a bug in a nested Suspense where the inner fallback itself suspends (via use() on a delay promise), and the inner content resolves before the fallback. Fizz mis-tracks boundary segments during the transition from "pending with suspended fallback" to "completed."

This is a useful pattern for when you want to create a `DeferredSuspense` boundary that blocks for a pre-set amount of time and then flushes. If the period passes and the children have not un-suspended, we flush the alternate boundary to the client.

I am aware this a cursed use of suspense, but it should be valid imo.


React version: 19.2.4

## Steps To Reproduce

1. `$ node nested-suspense-bug-repro.mjs`

Link to code example:

https://gist.github.com/switz/45d7c9f49953e11de7eec9d737841e2e#file-nested-suspense-bug-repro-mjs

## The current behavior

```
$ node nested-suspense-bug-repro.mjs
onError: A previously unvisited boundary must have exactly one root segment. This is a bug in React.
Bug triggered: A previously unvisited boundary must have exactly one root segment. This is a bug in React.
```

## The expected behavior

 When content resolves FAST (before ms):
  - No fallback is ever shown — content renders directly

  When content resolves SLOW (after ms):
  - For the first ms milliseconds, nothing visible changes (outer Suspense holds)
  - After ms, the fallback appears (inner Suspense fallback delay resolves, outer Suspense can now show its
   content which includes the pending inner boundary with its fallback)
  - When content finally resolves, it replaces the fallback via streaming

  The basic mechanics:
```
  <Suspense fallback={fallback}>              ← outer: catches if inner fallback suspends
    <Suspense fallback={<Delay ms={200}>{fallback}</Delay>}>  ← inner: delay on fallback
      {children}                               ← the actual async content
    </Suspense>
  </Suspense>
```

I stumbled across a strange bug that appears to be related to the React Compiler when extracting TanStack Table logic into a separate component that uses the Table instance.

I created a Pagination component that calls methods such as table.getCanNextPage() and table.getCanPreviousPage(), but by default it does not render correctly. title: Bug: ReactDOM.preloadModule crashes with repeated custom as value
body:
React version: current `main` (`d5736f098edee62c44f27b053e6e48f5fa443803` locally) ## Steps To Reproduce 1. Render a component on the server with two `ReactDOM.preloadModule()` calls that use the same non-default `as` value: ```js function App() { ReactDOM.preloadModule('worker-a', {as: 'serviceworker'}); ReactDOM.preloadModule('worker-b', {as: 'serviceworker'}); return
hello
; } renderToPipeableStream().pipe(writable); ``` 2. Let the Fizz render run. Link to code example: minimal reproduction above; this is also covered by the added regression test in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFloat-test.js`. ## The current behavior The second call crashes during server rendering: ```text TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'hasOwnProperty') ``` The repeated custom-`as` path checks `moduleUnknownResources` but then reads the bucket from `unknownResources`, so the bucket can be undefined. ## The expected behavior Fizz should track repeated custom module preload `as` values in `moduleUnknownResources` and emit both module preload links without crashing.

title: Protect react from AI slop PRs
body:
6 of 62 PRs in the last 2 weeks would have been auto-closed before review (e.g. #36402 Create heymit.txt, #36401 Add eduardo.txt with introduction text).

Install a GitHub Action:

- [PR Quality Gate](https://github.com/kimjune01/sweep/blob/master/action.yml), judges PR quality not authorship, lets competent bots through, blocks lazy humans

title: Bug: `fetchPriority` is not available in `ReactDOM.preloadModule()`
body:
`ReactDOM.preload()` supports a fetchPriority option, but `ReactDOM.preloadModule()` currently ignores
it, ruling out more granular preload optimization for ESM-based apps.

## Details

Frameworks using native ES modules rely on `modulepreload` to discover client-side JavaScript
during server rendering. By default, these get a high priority in browsers.

When a page emits many JS files, they may compete with render-critical resources.

React already fixes this for bootstrap modules via `fetchPriority="low"` and also It also supports explicit priorities through `ReactDOM.preload()` and `ReactDOM.preinit()` but *not* via `ReactDOM.preloadModule()`.

This would enable the optimization so `@vitejs/plugin-rsc` and others can pass `fetchPriority: 'low'` further down (see https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/pull/1264).

## Proposed Addition

Extend `PreloadModuleOptions` with `fetchPriority` and forward this value to the generated link.

```ts
type PreloadModuleOptions = {
  as?: string
  crossOrigin?: string
  integrity?: string
  nonce?: string
  fetchPriority?: 'high' | 'low' | 'auto'
}
```

The same option may also make sense for `ReactDOM.preinitModule()`.

## Alternatives

Developers could:

- Rewrite React’s streamed HTML (exhausting and brittle)
- Emit separate preload hints (risking duplication)
- Avoid early module discovery entirely (not performant)

## (Somewhat) related work

- #26826 
- #26880 
- #27189

title: Bug: SSR-streamed Suspense boundaries are never revealed while the document is hidden (first $RB flush waits on requestAnimationFrame; $~ opts the boundary out of client rendering)
body:
## React version

19.2.7 (also present on `main` in `packages/react-dom-bindings/src/server/fizz-instruction-set/ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetShared.js`)

## Summary

When an SSR-streamed page is loaded in a **hidden tab** (opened via cmd/ctrl+click, a restored background tab, or an automation-driven tab), streamed Suspense boundaries are never revealed: the completion segments arrive and sit in the DOM, `document.readyState` becomes `"complete"`, but the user-visible DOM shows the fallbacks indefinitely — until the tab becomes visible. React also does not client-render these boundaries, so nothing inside the page can recover on its own.

## Mechanism

In `completeBoundary` (`ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetShared.js`):

1. The boundary is marked queued — comment data set to `$~` (`SUSPENSE_QUEUED_START_DATA`) — *"so we know not to client render it at the end of document load"*, and the pair is pushed to `window.$RB`.
2. On the **first** push (`$RB.length === 2`), since `window.$RT` is not yet a number, the flush is scheduled with:

   ```js
   // If we haven't had our rAF callback yet, schedule everything for the first paint.
   requestAnimationFrame(window['$RV'].bind(null, window['$RB']));
   ```

3. Per spec, `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks do not run while the document is hidden — so `$RV` never runs and `$RT` is never set.
4. Every subsequent `completeBoundary` call pushes onto the still-unflushed `$RB` (`length > 2`, so no new scheduling happens). The `setTimeout` throttle path (which would fire even in hidden tabs) is only reachable once `$RT` has been set by a first flush.
5. On the hydration side, `isSuspenseInstancePending` treats `$~` as pending, so the client never falls back to client-rendering these boundaries at end of document load.

Net effect: a deadlock for the lifetime of the hidden state. The whole page's content is present in hidden `<div hidden id="S:n">` segments, but the visible DOM is fallbacks only.

## Observed evidence (production build, Next.

title: Bug: Importing `react-dom/server` under Deno prevents the process from ever exiting.
body:
Deno's export-condition resolution selects the **browser** server build, which creates a `MessageChannel` at module scope and assigns `port1.onmessage`. That refs the port against the event loop, and nothing ever closes it, so the runtime stays alive forever after the script finishes.

No rendering is required, because the channel is created at module scope. The equivalent Node import is unaffected, since `server.node.js` schedules on `setImmediate` and contains no `MessageChannel`.

React version: 19.2.8

(Tested against Deno 2.9.3 and Node 26.5.0)

## Steps To Reproduce

Setup `npm install react-dom@19.2.8`

- Case 1. `node -e "import 'react-dom/server'; console.log('done');"`
- Case 2. `deno eval "import 'react-dom/server'; console.log('done');"`
- Case 3. `deno eval "import 'react-dom/server.node'; console.log('done');"`

In all cases "done" is output.

However, under node (case 1), the process completes. Under deno, using 'react-dom/server' (case 2), the process hangs. Under deno, using 'react-dom/server.node' (case 3), the process completes.

## Is this a deno bug?

TL;DR: Not really, both node and deno act the same when given the same builds.

`react-dom`'s `./server` export map points the `deno` condition to the browser export:

```json
"./server": {
  "react-server": "./server.react-server.js",
  "workerd":      "./server.edge.js",
  "bun":          "./server.bun.js",
  "deno":         "./server.browser.js",
  "worker":       "./server.browser.js",
  "node":         "./server.node.js",
  "edge-light":   "./server.edge.js",
  "browser":      "./server.browser.js",
  "default":      "./server.node.js"
}
```

(Note that deno also sets the `node` condition, however the `deno` condition is listed first above so it wins)

Neither Deno nor react-dom misbehaves alone; it is specifically Deno resolving to the browser build.

The key difference between the builds is the construction of `MessageChannel`.

title: [Flight] Performance track debug info is not recovered for plain object roots
body:
## Summary

`flushComponentPerformance` reads `root._debugInfo` from the chunk. When
that array is empty and the chunk is fulfilled, it recovers the debug info
from the resolved value, but only when the value is an array, an async
iterable, a React element, or a lazy:

```js
if (debugInfo.length === 0 && root.status === 'fulfilled') {
  const resolvedValue = resolveLazy(root.value);
  if (
    typeof resolvedValue === 'object' && resolvedValue !== null &&
    (isArray(resolvedValue) ||
      typeof resolvedValue[ASYNC_ITERATOR] === 'function' ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_ELEMENT_TYPE ||
      resolvedValue.$$typeof === REACT_LAZY_TYPE) &&
    isArray(resolvedValue._debugInfo)
  ) {
    debugInfo = resolvedValue._debugInfo;
  }
}
```

A plain object root is excluded, so the Server Components track in the
Performance panel does not work for payloads whose root is a plain object,
even when the resolved value carries a `_debugInfo` array. Verified in
`react-server-dom-webpack@19.3.0-canary-28cd4bb0-20260723`.

## Context

Waku's RSC payload root is a plain object mapping slot ids to elements
(`Record<string, unknown>`), which lets one payload carry several named
elements. This shape is deliberate and we would like to keep it. Today we
patch the read site with a build transform that drops the type restriction,
which works but is coupled to the compiled output:

https://github.com/wakujs/waku/blob/main/packages/waku/src/lib/vite-plugins/patch-rsdw.ts

@vitejs/plugin-rsc documents the same shape constraint for its performance
track example (vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1152, vitejs/vite-plugin-react#1304).

## Request

Relax the recovery to accept any object value that carries an own
`_debugInfo` array. The type restriction seems to mirror
`moveDebugInfoFromChunkToInnerValue`, where it guards attaching
`_debugInfo` to the value. The read site only reads the property, so the
restriction does not appear to protect anything there, and the relaxation

title: Show usage against the plan limit for the current billing period
body: **Goal.** Someone opening Usage can tell how much of their plan they have used, without doing any arithmetic. **Problem.** The page reports totals for whichever window you picked. It never says how close you are to the plan limit. **Scope** - default to the current billing period - "% of plan consumed" as the headline, and as a tile - the usage bar, with the notification markers on it - cumulative usage against the plan limit, with the limit drawn as a ceiling. Billing periods only, see below - the slot under the meter for the line that explains the numbers. Its wording is a projection (#8188) or an overage consequence (#8187), so this issue builds the slot rather than the sentences Covers the healthy and approaching states. Over limit and restricted are #8187. **Not here** - the projected end-of-period figure, in the tile, the chart line and the slot. All #8188 - the period's dates, its reset date and days remaining. All #8258, because none of them can be read from the API today **Free plans** Measured over a trailing 30 days, so there is no period start and nothing to project to. They get the meter and daily volume rather than cumulative against a ceiling, because a rolling total can fall as old days drop out of the window. **No plan limit** Where there is no limit to divide by, show the total and no percentage. **Done when** someone on any plan can see how much of their allowance they have used.

title: Break usage down by request type or SDK
body: **Goal.** Someone who has seen how much they used can find out where it came from. **Problem.** The breakdown is a daily volume chart with By Endpoint and By SDK as separate tabs, so the four billable request types are never named as such. **Scope** - the breakdown gets its own section, with no plan limit on it, since an individual request type has no limit of its own - rename By Endpoint to By request type. The rows are the four billable types - a dimension menu: request type, SDK Both dimensions derive from the response the charts already fetch, so they cost no extra requests. Project and environment are split out into their own issue: each costs one request per key, and `usage-data` is throttled at 5/min per user, so a multi-project org gets 429s and a list that ranks the rest wrongly. **Decide here.** The menu covers the same ground as the existing tabs. If it replaces them, removing the old By SDK view and its sidebar is part of this work rather than left behind as dead code. **Done when** - the breakdown renders per dimension, and carries no limit line - either the old tabs are gone, or there is a written reason they stayed

body:
**Goal.** Build the states shown when an organisation goes past its plan limit, so it can see what happened, what it means and what restores normal service.

**Problem.** Neither state exists. The restricted one is unreachable anyway: a restricted organisation is sent to the blocked screen on every route except the organisations list, so the page that would explain it is the one page they cannot open.

title: Show projected end-of-period usage
body: **Goal.** See where usage is heading before the period ends, while there is still time to act. Today the page only shows what has already happened. **Build.** One calculation, two places: - a **dashed line** on the chart, from today to the period end - a **sentence under the meter**, like "On track to use ~1.9M (94% of your limit) by 17 Aug", or that it lands over the limit **Hide it early in the period**, where an average means very little. Pick the point: a number of days, or a share of the period. **Never on a rolling window.** Free plans have no period end to project to, and their total can fall as old days drop out, so a projection there is misleading rather than merely early. **Call it an estimate.** A straight-line average of usage so far, not a forecast. **Needs #8257.** The projection divides by the period length, which the API does not return today. **Done when** - the projection appears in both places once there is enough of the period to mean anything, and in neither before - a projection that lands over the limit is obvious without working it out

title: OAuth Dynamic client registration rejects client names containing colons
body:
Sentry Issue: [FLAGSMITH-API-6BB](https://flagsmith.sentry.io/issues/7644734336/?referrer=github_integration)

`POST /o/register/` rejects a client whose `client_name` contains a colon with `invalid_client_metadata`:

```
client_name:  Claude Code (plugin:core-tools:flagsmith)
redirect_uris: ["http://localhost:3118/callback"]
user_agent:   claude-code/2.1.220 (sdk-cli)

{"error": "invalid_client_metadata",
 "error_description": "Client name may only contain letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, underscores, dots, and parentheses."}
```

RFC 7591 § 2 places no constraints on `client_name`, and § 2.2 provides for localised names. The allowlist also rejects any name outside ASCII, so a client called `フラグスミス` or `Müller GmbH` cannot register either.

Rejecting conformant metadata makes our DCR endpoint non-conformant.

title: Slow DB Query: org permission check takes ~2.6s on GET /organisations/{id}/groups/
body:
**Sentry:** [FLAGSMITH-API-6BK](https://flagsmith.sentry.io/issues/7649995740/)

### User impact
`GET /api/v1/organisations/{organisation_pk}/groups/` takes **~2.6 seconds**, and
users feel all of it — the org Groups page just sits there loading.

- **14 users affected**, 16 occurrences
- First seen 2026-08-03T16:38Z, **still occurring** (last seen 2026-08-05T16:04Z)
- Not an error — nothing breaks, it's purely slow. This is why it was classified
  `info`/`low` by Sentry and initially archived.

### Where the time goes
One span accounts for essentially the whole request:

| Span | Duration |
|---|---|
| `db` — org permission check (below) | **2599 ms** |
| `db` — count user permission groups | 3 ms |
| remaining 8 spans | 1 ms each |

### The query
An org-level permission check that `LEFT OUTER JOIN`s the entire RBAC graph —
`userorganisationpermission` (+ its permissions M2M), `userpermissiongroup`
(+ users, + its org-permissions M2M), `rbac_role`, `rbac_userrole`,
`rbac_grouprole`, `rbac_roleorganisationpermission` (+ its permissions M2M) —
then `WHERE … LIMIT 1`:

```sql
SELECT %s AS "a" FROM "organisations_organisation"
LEFT OUTER JOIN "organisation_permissions_userorganisationpermission" …
LEFT OUTER JOIN "users_userpermissiongroup" …
LEFT OUTER JOIN "rbac_role" …
LEFT OUTER JOIN "rbac_userrole" …
LEFT OUTER JOIN "rbac_grouprole" …
LEFT OUTER JOIN "rbac_roleorganisationpermission" …
INNER JOIN "organisations_userorganisation" …
WHERE (… user_id = %s … OR … OR …) AND organisation_id = %s LIMIT 1
```

### Suggested direction
It only needs to answer "does this user hold this permission on this org?", but
builds a full cross-product of three independent permission paths (direct,
group, role) before discarding all but one row. Splitting it into three cheap
`EXISTS` checks short-circuited with `OR`, or a `UNION ALL … LIMIT 1`, would
avoid the join explosion. Worth checking indexes on the RBAC join columns too.

### Triage note
Initially archived `--until auto` by the

title: Status text on tinted surfaces fails WCAG AA contrast
body:
**Goal.** Status text on a tinted status surface is readable, and passes WCAG AA.

**Problem.** The semantic pairs fail. Measured in light mode:

| Pair | Ratio | AA body text needs 4.5:1 |
|---|---|---|
| `text-warning` on `surface-warning` | 1.93:1 | fails |
| `text-success` on `surface-success` | 2.64:1 | fails |
| `text-danger` on `surface-danger` | 3.25:1 | fails, passes large text only |

It is not only the pairing. `text-warning` is 2.04:1 on plain white, so it fails as body text on any light background.

Already shipping with these pairs: `experiments/StatusBadge`, `MetricsComparisonTable`, `WizardStepper`, `WarehouseSetup`, `SetupStep`.

**Why the surface cannot be the fix.** The surfaces are 8% tints, so they are nearly white already. Even against pure white all three fail. Fixing via surfaces means inverting to dark surfaces with light text, which is a redesign rather than a token change.

**Scope**

- darker text values for the three statuses. These clear 4.5:1 on their own tint: warning `#b45800`, danger `#dc141f`, success `#1c7d6d`
- leave `border-*` and `icon-*` at the brand colours. Non-text contrast only needs 3:1, so the brand orange, teal and red survive wherever they are decorative
- measure and set dark mode separately. The text tokens are currently identical in both themes while the surfaces are not, so darkening globally would make dark mode worse
- a comment in the token file saying why text and border diverge, or someone will tidy them back together

**Done when**

- all three pairs clear 4.5:1 in both themes
- the five components above are checked against the new values
- large display numbers still read as intended, since they only need 3:1 and will now be darker

Two booleans per organisation, on the response the usage page already fetches:

- **can this organisation be cut off?** Restriction is switched on per organisation and some are exempt

The usage page can show how much of a plan has been used, but not when the allowance resets. The billing period is never returned, so there is nothing to put on screen.

body: **Goal.** Someone can see which billing period they are in, when their allowance resets, and how long is left. Three things on the usage page describe the period itself, and none can be read from the API today: - the period's date range - when the allowance resets - days remaining Needs #8257. title: Display the grace period state on the dashboard
body:
**Goal.** A paid customer over their plan limit knows whether it is costing them money.

We do not charge for the first billing month an organisation goes between 100% and 200% of its limit. Every month over after that is charged as overage. That first month is the **grace period**, the name used throughout the codebase and on the page.

So an organisation sitting at 118% is in one of two situations, and the page cannot currently tell them apart:

- **covered**, nothing to pay this month
- **charged**, at the overage rate

**Where it appears**

- the over-limit banner
- the line under the meter
- the existing quota warning, which today says "automated billing for the overages may apply" because it cannot tell either

Needs #8256, which returns whether the covered month has been used.

**Done when** an organisation at 118% is told whether it is being charged, and nothing on the page hedges.

title: Multivariate override editor hides the identity's override value (shows the flag's control value instead)
body:
## Description

When an identity has a single-value override on a feature that is later made multivariate, the "Edit User Feature" modal stops showing the identity's override value. In multivariate mode the editor renders only the flag's options as radios (control + each variant), so an override whose value is not one of those options has nowhere to appear. The control row shows the _environment's_ control value, so the identity looks like it is on the default.

The override is intact and the SDK serves it correctly, so this is a display issue in the override editor. If the user saves that modal, the displayed control value is written over the override, so the value can be lost on save.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a standard flag with control value `ENV_DEFAULT`.

3. On the Features page, make the feature multivariate: update the control value and add a variant `VARIANT_A`.
4. Open that identity and open the "Edit User Feature" modal for the flag.

The editor shows the identity's override value (`MY_OVERRIDE`).

The editor shows the flag's control value selected. `MY_OVERRIDE` is not shown anywhere in the modal. The identities list still shows `MY_OVERRIDE`, and the SDK still serves it.

## Screenshots

- **Identities list (correct):** the feature row shows the override `MY_OVERRIDE`.
- **Edit User Feature modal (the bug):** only `ENV_DEFAULT` (selected) and `VARIANT_A` are shown; `MY_OVERRIDE` is absent.
- **Features page:** the flag's control value and variation as configured.

## Impact

Display only, no data lost while viewing. Risk: saving the modal overwrites the override with the displayed control value.

## Root cause (initial)

`frontend/web/components/modals/create-feature/tabs/FeatureValueTab.tsx` passes the environment control value as `controlValue` to `VariationOptions` in select mode (changed in #6585, which fixed #6582). The multivariate override editor only models "cont

title: UI can't manage some segments
body:
Originally, we conceived the segment rules data model so that the frontend would only send a sandwich-like ruleset, in which:
- The root rule has no conditions; rather, it's an `ALL` rule housing subrules.
- Subrules of the root rule must own conditions, but could have no subrules.

The API wouldn't imply any restrictions to the shape of a ruleset, so none of these matter when managing segments via the API. However, this means that _**our UI cannot manage _some_ segments**_ our customer created/updated via the API, because of being incompatible to their ruleset shape.

Some interesting timeline to keep in mind:

- https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith/issues/5769 — `SegmentSerializer` skips any rules nested deeper than a second level — which arguably makes it worse, as there's no error raised to inform the requester.
- https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith/issues/7400 — The frontend was made compatible with `ANY` root rules.
- https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith/issues/7815, https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith/issues/7818 — `Segment.rules` became a JSON field, which greatly simplified the multiple parts of the system dealing with segment rules. `SegmentSerializer` was improved to **reject** rules nested too deep, and typing was improved a notch.

The goal of this issue is to yet again simplify segments.

## Acceptance criteria

- The frontend can manage segment rules and their conditions given any shape — it might need a major redesign of managing rules.
- The backend loses all logic that restrict or imply that rules cannot be nested, or cannot have conditions, at any nesting level, in all segment write paths.

title: Emit CLI usage events from an API middleware
body:
Add middleware to `api/telemetry/middleware.py`, emitting `cli.request.made` once per authenticated CLI request. The middleware holds no state and reads no cache or database.

### Acceptance criteria

- A request whose user-agent matches the CLI pattern, from an authenticated user, emits `cli.request.made` at INFO on the `cli` logger with `cli.version`, `cli.os`, `cli.arch`, `organisation.id`, `status` and `amplitude.user_id`.
- `amplitude.user_id` is `str(request.user.uuid)`.
- `status` is `error` when the response status code is 400 or above, `success` otherwise. The event is emitted after the response is obtained, so a 500 is still recorded.
- A master API key request emits the event with `organisation.id` resolved from the key's organisation. `organisation.id` resolution logic mirrors, or reuses, `MCPUsageLoggerMiddleware`.
- An unauthenticated request emits nothing, whatever its user-agent.

title: First evaluation never reported for compressed environment documents
body:
`_get_compressed_environment_document` in Core validates the mapped environment document against the `flagsmith_schemas.dynamodb` TypedDicts before writing to DynamoDB. Pydantic's TypedDict validation strips unknown keys, and `onboarding_pending` was never declared here — so it has been silently dropped from every compressed document since the onboarding feature shipped in Core v2.256.0.

The result in production: 0 of 51,125 documents in `flagsmith_environments` carry `onboarding_pending`, the Edge API never sees pending onboarding state, and the `environment.first_evaluated` event is never sent for environments served via Edge.

title: Deep-linked feature value renders as [object Object]
body:
Opening a flag via a **deep-link** (`…/features?feature=<id>`) renders its value as **`[object Object]`** in the editor. Opening the same flag by clicking into it from the Features list shows the correct value.

**Root cause:** the two paths read the value from different endpoints with different shapes.
- Feature-list (normal path): `environment_feature_state` is serialised by `FeatureStateSerializerSmall` → `get_feature_state_value()` → a **flat** value (e.g. a string).
- Deep-link path: `useDeepLinkedFeature` → `useGetFeatureStatesQuery` (`features/featurestates/`), whose `feature_state_value` is the **nested** object `{type, string_value, integer_value, boolean_value}`.

`pickEnvironmentFlag` (`web/components/pages/features/hooks/deepLinkedFeature.ts`) passes that nested object straight through, so the value editor stringifies it to `[object Object]`. Confirmed against the live `featurestates` response (value returned as `{type:"unicode", string_value:"…"}`).

**Not display-only:** the edit view shows the same bad value, so saving (even with no changes) would persist `[object Object]` over the real value. The stored value is currently correct; the risk is on save.

**Repro:** deep-link to a JSON-valued flag that sits **beyond the first page** of the list (`FEATURES_PAGE_SIZE = 50`) — that triggers the `useDeepLinkedFeature` fetch of `features/featurestates/`. Flags on page 1 use the list's flat value and render fine.

title: Bug: [Flight] Unbounded _debugInfo growth in transferReferencedDebugInfo throws RangeError: Invalid array length
body:
## Environment

- `next@16.2.10`, which bundles `react-server-dom-turbopack` at
  `19.3.0-experimental-3f0b9e61-20260317`
- Also verified unchanged in `next@16.3.2` (`19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731`)
  and `next@16.4.0-canary.1` (`19.3.0-canary-eafeac09-20260819`)
- Dev mode only. The production client bundle contains no `_debugInfo` and is unaffected.
- App: Payload CMS 3.87 admin. Inserting a Lexical block whose field subtree is large
  reproduces it every time; smaller blocks in the same editor never do.

## What happens

Inserting the block triggers a server action whose RSC response is a large, heavily
deduplicated model graph. The client throws:

    RangeError: Invalid array length
        at Array.push (<anonymous>)
        at rejectReference (react-server-dom-turbopack-client.browser.development.js)
        at fulfillReference (...)
        at initializeModelChunk (...)
        at resolveModelChunk (...)

The error surfaces in the error boundary around the field. The underlying error is lost.

## Why

`transferReferencedDebugInfo` copies every `name == null` entry from the referenced chunk's
`_debugInfo` into the parent chunk's. Because each chunk's accumulated entries are copied
again into every chunk that references it, the arrays grow superlinearly with graph depth and
the amount of reference deduplication. Eventually `parentChunk.push` exceeds V8's limit for
pointer-element arrays (2^27 = 134,217,728) and throws `RangeError: Invalid array length`.

That RangeError is caught by `fulfillReference`, which calls `rejectReference`. `rejectReference`
then does `handler._debugInfo.push(erroredComponent)` on the same maxed-out array, throwing the
identical RangeError a second time — this time uncaught. So the reported error is React's own
error path failing, and the original error never reaches the user.

## Measurements

Instrumenting `transferReferencedDebugInfo` with a length cap in the dev bundle:

- plain admin page load: parent `_debugInfo` reaches ~21,0

In development builds, `react-server-dom-*-client.*.development.js` calls `Object.freeze(element.props)` when an element is initialised (`initializeElement`). Later, `fulfillReference()` writes a resolved reference into its parent object with a plain assignment:

"__proto__" !== key && (parentObject[key] = mappedValue);
```

Whether the reference resolves before or after the freeze depends on chunk arrival order, so the failure is intermittent (worse on a cold dev server). Production bundles do not freeze, so it never reproduces there.

title: Meter compares the selected period against a 30-day allowance
body:
The meter shows usage as a percentage of the plan limit, but the limit and the period being viewed do not always measure the same span.

`max_api_calls` is `allowed_30d_api_calls`: a 30-day allowance.

| Period on screen | What the percentage means |
| --- | --- |
| Last 30 days | correct |
| Last 90 days | roughly 3x overstated |
| Current billing period | correct only where the term is monthly |

So on "Last 90 days" an organisation reads "55% of plan consumed" from 27.6M against 50M, when the 50M covers 30 days.

Raised on #8320, where the chart was fixed to follow the period being viewed. The meter was not.

## Options

- **Show the percentage only where the comparison holds**, and otherwise show the total with the allowance labelled. A missing percentage is better than a wrong one.
- **Pro-rata the allowance to the period**, clearly marked indicative.
- **Label the allowance**, e.g. "50M / 30 days", and let the reader do the arithmetic.

Needs a product call rather than an engineering one, and it interacts with #8188: a projection divides by the period length, so both want the same answer about what the allowance covers.

## Done when

The meter never states a percentage that compares two different spans.

title: Meter divides one project's usage by the organisation's allowance
body:
Filtering by project scopes the usage total but not the allowance, so the meter divides one project's calls by the whole organisation's limit and calls the result "% of plan consumed".

`total` comes from the usage query, which takes `projectId`. `limit` is `max_api_calls`, which is organisation-wide. Nothing on the meter says a filter is applied.


## Options

- **Separate the project selector from the allowance**, so the meter always reports the organisation and the filter only drives the chart and the breakdown.
- **Reword it for the filtered case**, e.g. "Project '<name>' contributed X% of your overall plan allowance", and make the applied filter obvious.

Either way the meter should not present a scoped numerator against an unscoped denominator without saying so.

Related to #8353, which is the same defect along a different axis: there the numerator and denominator cover different periods, here different scopes.

## Done when

The meter either reports the organisation regardless of the filter, or states plainly that it is showing one project's contribution to the organisation's allowance.

title: Usage page can spin indefinitely when a request never settles
body:
The Flagsmith organisation with the "Disabled Flags" project selected shows a spinner that never resolves.

## Why it can hang

`isLoading` is `loadingOrganisation || loadingUsage || loadingLimit`. There is no upper bound on any of them. A request that never settles, rather than failing, leaves the page spinning with nothing to say.

A request that *errors* is handled: `isError` renders "Usage could not be loaded". The gap is a request that neither resolves nor rejects, or one slow enough to look that way.

## What to do

- find out what the usage endpoint does for that project, since a response that never arrives is a backend problem first
- give the page a way out regardless: after some threshold, say the data is taking longer than expected rather than spinning indefinitely
- an indefinite spinner is the least useful state on the page, and it is the one we currently fall into by default

## Done when

No combination of organisation and project leaves the page spinning with no explanation.

title: Group organisation usage by project and environment in one request
body:
The usage dashboard can break usage down by request type and SDK, but not by project or environment. Those two need one request per key, and `GET /organisations/{id}/usage-data/` is throttled at five a minute per user, so any organisation with a handful of projects gets 429s.

The SDK dimension has no such problem because rows in `events_list` already carry `labels.user_agent`, so the frontend groups them client side off the one request the page has already made. Project and environment want the same shape.

**What we need.** One response that carries the per project and per environment split, rather than the caller asking once per key. Either:

- add project and environment to the labels on each row, so the existing client side grouping picks them up, or
- add `group_by=project|environment` returning one row per key

Whichever fits the analytics service better. The frontend only needs to be able to rank projects by usage without making N requests.

**Where things are**

- `api/app_analytics/views.py`, `get_usage_data_view`, carries `@throttle_classes([InfluxQueryThrottle])`
- `api/app_analytics/throttles.py`, scope `influx_query`, keyed on `user.pk`
- `api/app/settings/common.py`, `"influx_query": "5/min"`
- `api/app_analytics/serializers.py`, `UsageDataQuerySerializer` takes `project_id` and `environment_id` as filters today
- Both the Influx and Postgres paths in `api/app_analytics/analytics_db_service.py` would need it

**Why now.** #8186 shipped the breakdown with request type and SDK only. The project and environment dimensions are held back until this lands: a throttled scope reports nothing, and a breakdown that silently omits a project ranks the remaining ones wrongly.

title: Break usage down by project and environment
body:
The usage breakdown ships with request type and SDK (#8186). Project and environment were held back because each costs one request per key, and `usage-data` is throttled at 5/min per user, so a multi-project org gets 429s and a list that ranks the rest wrongly.

Once the endpoint can return the split in one response, add both dimensions back:

- project and environment entries in `BREAKDOWN_DIMENSIONS`
- environment depends on a selected project, so the dimension needs to ask for one first
- a scope that fails must not read as zero usage, and the list must not sit loading when one never answers

The last point covers two bugs found in the first implementation, so they are worth designing out rather than rediscovering.

The removed implementation is in the #8343 branch history, taken out in `4f84749`.

Blocked by #8361.

title: Add a shared TraitValue type instead of casting value_type
body:
Follow-up to [#8344](https://github.com/Flagsmith/flagsmith/pull/8344), from Wadii's review comment there.

`featureStateToValue` reads the type key off two different API shapes, and reaches for an assertion to do it:

```ts
const type =
  (value as { value_type?: FeatureStateValue['type'] }).value_type ?? value.type
```

`value_type` is invented at the call site, so it is tied to nothing and a rename is silent.

Naming the trait shape lets `in` narrow instead:

```ts
// responses.ts
export type TraitValue = {
  boolean_value: boolean | null
  float_value?: number | null
  integer_value: number | null
  string_value: string | null
  value_type: 'int' | 'unicode' | 'bool' | 'float'
}

// featureStateToValue.ts
value: FlagsmithValue | FeatureStateValue | TraitValue | undefined
const type = 'value_type' in value ? value.value_type : value.type
```

`float_value` and `'float'` are in there because traits carry both (`api/environments/identities/traits/models.py:15,37`).

The half that actually catches renames is the producer: `Utils.valueToTrait` (`utils.tsx:887`) builds this same object with no return annotation, so annotate it `: TraitValue`. Checked locally, renaming the key then fails in both places instead of neither.

Kept out of #8344 because it pulls `utils.tsx` back into a PR whose point was decoupling from it.

MCP tool calls always return 401 on v2.271.0: django-oauth-toolkit 3.4 rejects resource-bound OAuth tokens
body:
### How are you running Flagsmith

- [ ] Self Hosted with Docker
- [ ] Self Hosted with Kubernetes
- [ ] SaaS at flagsmith.com
- [x] Some other way (add details in description below)

### Describe the bug

Self-hosted v2.271.0: official `flagsmith/flagsmith` and `flagsmith/flagsmith-mcp:2.271.0` images on a Kubernetes-based PaaS (not the Helm chart), TLS terminated at the ingress.

The MCP OAuth flow completes (dynamic client registration, authorize and token exchange all return 2xx), but every tool call fails. The MCP server forwards the bearer token, and the API answers `401 {"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}`, even with a token issued seconds earlier.

**Cause.** #8469 (lock file refresh) moved `django-oauth-toolkit` from 3.1.0 to 3.4.1, which the `>=3.0.1,<4.0.0` constraint allows. DOT 3.4.0 added RFC 8707 audience checks: `validate_bearer_token` now rejects a resource-bound token unless `allows_audience(request.uri)` passes. Two things make that fail:

1. MCP clients request tokens with `resource=<MCP server URL>`, as the MCP spec requires, and the MCP server forwards that token to the API (`mcp/src/flagsmith_mcp/auth.py`). The token's audience is the MCP server, not the API.
2. With DOT's Django backend, `request.uri` comes from `request.get_full_path()` and is path-only. The default `RESOURCE_SERVER_TOKEN_RESOURCE_VALIDATOR` (`validate_resource_as_url_prefix`) only matches absolute URIs, so it returns `False` even for a token bound to the API's own URL.

Checked inside the `2.271.0` image:

```
uri DOT passes to the audience check: '/api/v1/organisations/'
validate_resource_as_url_prefix('/api/v1/organisations/', ['https://<api-host>'])                     -> False
validate_resource_as_url_prefix('https://<api-host>/api/v1/organisations/', ['https://<api-host>'])   -> True
```

So on 2.271.0, any resource-bound token is rejected by the API as long as the default validator is used. 2.270.0 ships DOT 3.1.0, which has no audience check.

title: fix: a failed save leaves the button stuck with no error
body:
When a save fails, the button can stay disabled on "Updating" / "Creating Change Request" forever with no error. Only a reload clears it. Reported twice from production.

**1. Identity saves have no error handling.** `common/stores/identity-store.js` has four `store.saving()` calls and one `.catch`, and that one is in `getIdentity`, a load. So a failed PUT never resets `isSaving`. Every other store has more handlers than saves (account 8/16, feature-list 4/13, project 2/7, organisation 4/5).

**2. The identity editor ignores tag-scoped permissions.** `PUT .../edge-featurestates/{uuid}/` returns 403 when the user has `UPDATE_FEATURE_STATE` but isn't scoped to the feature's tags (`api/features/permissions.py:187`). It succeeds on one feature and fails on the next, so it reads as intermittent.

**3. Change requests fail the same way.** A flag value over the 20,000 character limit leaves "Creating Change Request" greyed out, with nothing saying the limit exists. `feature-list-store.ts` does have handlers, so this is a different mechanism and needs its own trace.

## Suggested fix

Two halves, both needed.

**Prevent what we can predict.** Disable the save with a tooltip saying why. The convention already exists: `Utils.renderWithPermission` wraps an element in a tooltip naming the missing permission, and `FlagValueFooter` pairs it with `<Permission tags={projectFlag?.tags}>` for the tag-scoped check. The identity footer just doesn't use either. Same for the character limit, which is knowable before the request.

**Handle what we can't.** A disabled button is a client-side guess at what the server will allow. It can't cover a throttle, a 500, a network drop, or any rule the frontend doesn't model, and those still hang today. `.catch((e) => API.ajaxHandler(store, e))` on the `identity-store.js` save paths resets `isSaving` and surfaces the message.

## Reproducing

The hang, without a real failure: open an identity's flag, DevTools → Network → Block request URL on `*/edge

body:
### Website or app

React DevTools standalone package: https://github.com/react/react/tree/main/packages/react-devtools-core

### Repro steps

### Version

`react-devtools-core@8.0.0`

### Problem

The published `dist/standalone.js` contains a frozen copy of `ws@7.5.10`.
`react-devtools-core` declares `ws` as `^7`, and a fresh npm installation now
resolves that external dependency to `ws@7.5.13`, but the standalone server
executes the copy compiled into its bundle instead.

The current repository lockfile resolves `ws@^7` to 7.5.10. The lockfile entry
before #37029 also resolved both `ws@^7` and `ws@^7.4.6` to 7.5.10, so this was
not introduced by the Playwright update.

This is relevant because the upstream fragment-memory fix was released in
`ws@7.5.11`. The upstream advisory and fix are already public:
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p

### Verification

1. Install the published package:

   ```console
   npm init -y
   npm install react-devtools-core@8.0.0
   ```

2. Inspect `node_modules/react-devtools-core/dist/standalone.js.map`.

3. Compare its 13 `node_modules/ws` `sourcesContent` entries with the published
   `ws@7.5.10` source files. All 13 match byte-for-byte. In particular, the
   following files remain in their 7.5.10 form and differ from 7.5.11:

   - `lib/receiver.js`
   - `lib/websocket-server.js`
   - `lib/websocket.js`

4. The compiled standalone artifact also lacks the

5. A fresh dependency resolution installs `ws@7.5.13`, but changing or
   overriding that external package does not change `dist/standalone.js`.

### Expected behavior

The published standalone artifact should be built with a patched supported
7.x release of `ws`.

### Suggested fix

Update `ws` to 7.5.11 or later, regenerate `dist/standalone.js`, and publish a
new `react-devtools-core` release containing the rebuilt artifact. Updating the
lockfile alone will not change the copy already frozen

body:
Tracking issue for the fix and data repair for #8397, where deleting an identity while an override is being written leaves the override behind in `environments_v2`.

Identity documents in `flagsmith_identities` are written by two services — this repo (`EdgeIdentity.save()`) and the Edge API (`update_identity` / `update_identities`) — and both do an unconditional whole-document `put_item` with no concurrency control. The `environments_v2` override documents are maintained separately, from a changeset diffed against the document *as read*, so a write landing between another request's read and its write is invisible to that request's diff and its override document is never cleaned up. Once the identity is gone or its uuid has changed, nothing can reach the stale document: it is keyed on an identity uuid that no longer resolves, so it cannot be removed through the API or the dashboard.

This is not only cosmetic. Where an environment has `use_identity_overrides_in_local_eval` enabled, the Edge API builds `identity_overrides` for the environment document straight from these `environments_v2` documents, so a local-evaluation SDK applies a stale override while remote evaluation — which reads the identity document — does not. The same flag, the same identifier, two answers depending on SDK mode.

### Optimistic concurrency control

Both writers need to participate. Neither change is useful alone, and each must be deployed before the other starts *writing* the attribute, because both sides' Pydantic models silently drop attributes they don't know about and would wipe it on the next write.

- [ ] **edge-api** — add `version` to its `IdentityModel` and round-trip it, so a document carrying the attribute survives an Edge API write untouched.
- [ ] **flagsmith** — add `version` to `IdentityModel` / the identity document mappers and round-trip it likewise.
- [ ] **edge-api** — bump `version` on every identity write and make the write conditional (`attribute_not_exists(version) OR

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/unrevised6419/next-turbopack-type-commonjs

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm dlx create-next-app@latest repro --ts --app --turbopack`
2. Add one line to `package.json`:
   ```json
   "type": "commonjs"
   ```
3. `pnpm exec next build`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** Turbopack fails to compile every file under `app/`, including the
untouched files `create-next-app` just generated:

```
> Build error occurred
Error: Turbopack build failed with 2 errors:
./app/layout.tsx
Error: Specified module format (CommonJs) is not matching the module format of the source code (EcmaScript Modules)
The CommonJs module format was specified in the package.json that is affecting this source file or by using an special extension, but Ecmascript import/export syntax is used in the source code.
The module was automatically converted to an EcmaScript module, but that is in conflict with the specified module format.

./app/page.tsx
Error: Specified module format (CommonJs) is not matching the module format of the source code (EcmaScript Modules)
```

`next dev` is affected too — `GET /` returns HTTP 500 with the same errors.

**Expected:** the build succeeds. `next build --webpack` on the *same*
`package.json` compiles fine, so this is Turbopack-specific.

Worth noting: *omitting* `type` is not equivalent to setting it to
`"commonjs"`. Node treats both as CommonJS, but Turbopack only enforces the
format when the field is explicit — so the field is load-bearing in a way that
is invisible until you add it.

**Generated server-action entries hit this too.** Add a `"use server"` module

title: [turbopack] after a file changes, loaders are first run with the file's previous content
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/stefanprobst/next-turbopack-loader-stale-source-repro

### To Reproduce

pnpm install
node repro.mjs          # edit styles/index.css, turbopack
node repro.mjs --txt    # edit app/message.txt, turbopack
node repro.mjs --webpack
node repro.mjs --webpack --txt


see https://github.com/stefanprobst/next-turbopack-loader-stale-source-repro/blob/main/README.md

### Current vs. Expected behavior

In `next dev` with Turbopack, editing a file that goes through a loader (configured in `turbopack.rules`) runs the loader chain **twice**. The first call gets the file's **previous** content, although the file on disk already has the new content. The second call gets the current content. `next dev --webpack` runs the loader once, with the current content.

The final output is correct as long as the loader only looks at the `source` it's given. Loaders that also read the file system see a disk state that doesn't match their input. A loader that caches by the file's mtime (as `@tailwindcss/turbopack` does) rebuilds its cache from the stale content in the first call, sees an unchanged mtime in the second call, and reuses the stale result. The served output then always lags one edit behind.

This looks like the same underlying problem as #93052, which describes it for the built-in PostCSS transform and only when a PostCSS plugin reports a dependency. This repro shows it's broader:

- it happens for any loader in `turbopack.rules`, not just PostCSS;
- the loader here reports no dependencies;
- it's not CSS-specific: a `*.txt` file loaded `as: "*.js"` behaves the same.

title: cacheHandlers[*].updateTags only receives the first profile group when one request revalidates tags with different profiles
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/uaoa/next-updatetags-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo, run `npm install`, `npx next build`, `npx next start -p 3457`.
2. Open http://localhost:3457 and click "Revalidate a and b".
3. The server action in `app/actions.ts` calls, in one request:

   updateTag('a');
   revalidateTag('b', { expire: 0 });

4. Watch the server log. `cache-handler.mjs` wraps Next's own `createDefaultCacheHandler`
   and only logs every `updateTags(tags, durations)` call.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: the custom cache handler's `updateTags` is called only with `["a"]`. Tag `b` never reaches it:

  [cache-handler] updateTags ["a"] null

Expected: `updateTags` is called once per profile group:

  [cache-handler] updateTags ["a"] null
  [cache-handler] updateTags ["b"] {"expire":0}

With the built-in handler the bug is invisible, because `b` is still invalidated locally through the shared
tags manifest. It shows up with any custom handler that relies on `updateTags`, e.g. one that propagates
invalidations across instances (Redis). In a multi-instance deployment `b` then stays stale on every
other instance.

Cause: in `dist/server/revalidation-utils.js`, `const handlers = getCacheHandlers()` returns
`handlersSet.values()` (a one-shot iterator; a generator in dev). The loop over profile groups consumes it
in the first group, so every later group iterates an empty iterator.
Suggested fix: `const handlers = Array.from(getCacheHandlers() ?? [])`.


### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:

title: System segments and their overrides can be modified by users
body:
System segments are hidden from the segments API, but their overrides aren't protected from user writes. They show up in the feature's Segment Overrides tab and behave like any other override: users can toggle, edit, reorder or remove them. The override APIs don't check `is_system_segment`, and the frontend doesn't read it.

Project change requests can also rewrite rules for system segments.

The following features are impacted:
- Flag dependencies
- Experiments
- Phased rollouts (release pipelines)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a flag dependency, or launch an experiment rollout.
2. Open the feature → Segment Overrides.
3. Toggle or remove the system segment's override, then click Update Segment Overrides. The change saves successfully.

With change requests:

- `POST /api/v1/environments/{key}/create-change-request/` with `feature_states: [{feature_segment: <system override>, enabled: true}]`, then commit: the override is flipped.
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/change-requests/` with `segments: [{version_of: <system segment id>, rules: [...]}]`, then commit: the system segment's rules are replaced.

### Proposed scope

- API: refuse changes to segments, and their overrides on system segments through the generic feature segment and feature state endpoints. The owning services (dependencies, experiments, release pipelines) should manage them. Affected endpoints:

| Endpoint | Used by |
|---|---|
| `PUT/PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/features/feature-segments/{id}/` | UI remove (non-versioned) |
| `POST /api/v1/features/feature-segments/update-priorities/` | UI reorder |
| `PUT/PATCH /api/v1/features/featurestates/{id}/` | UI toggle/value (non-versioned) |
| `POST /api/v1/environments/{env_id}/features/{feature_id}/versions/` (`feature_states_to_update`, `segment_ids_to_delete_overrides`) | UI (v2 versioning) |
| `POST /api/v1/environments/{key}/features/{feature_id}/create-segment-override/` | API |
| `POST /api/experiments/environments/{key}/update-flag-v1/` | API |
| `PO

title: Draft Mode doesn't isolate concurrent invocations of a `'use cache'` function
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/reimerwilliam/repro-use-cache-draft-mode-dedupe

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repro, then `pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start`
2. In another terminal, `node test-repro.mjs`

The script will enable draft mode, then run two overlapping requests for the same `'use cache'` key.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected**, per the Draft Mode docs:

> all functions and components under a caching directive scope re-execute on
> every request and results are not saved to the cache

**Current:** a Draft Mode request re-executes only when no other request is
already filling that cache key. If one is, it's handed that request's result
instead.

Next.js shares a single in-flight `'use cache'` fill between concurrent requests
for the same key, so a burst of traffic does the work once. Draft Mode isn't part
of that decision, and isn't part of the key the in-flight map uses, so a preview
request and a normal request end up sharing one fill.

Concretely: an author saves a change and clicks preview. If another request for
that page was mid-fetch at that moment, the preview shows the content from before
the save. A reload fixes it.

title: Dependency overrides serve a stale value while the prerequisite is off
body:
A dependency override copies the dependent feature's environment default value and variants when it's created, and doesn't track later changes to them. While the prerequisite isn't enabled, SDKs serve the dependent feature as disabled, with the value from when the dependency was created. Users reading the value regardless of the enabled state get stale data.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create `egg` with value `"wild egg"`, and make it depend on `chicken`, which is disabled.
2. Change `egg`'s environment default value to `"farm egg"`.
3. Evaluate flags: `egg` is disabled with value `"wild egg"`.

### Proposed scope

- When mapping dependent flags for evaluation, they take their value and variants from the feature's current environment default, not from the override's stored feature state value.
- Apply it in both places that map flags for evaluation, through a shared helper:
  - `api/evaluation/mappers.py:map_environment_to_evaluation_context` for the Core API SDK endpoints
  - `api/util/mappers/engine.py:map_environment_to_engine` for local eval and Edge API
- Identify dependency overrides by their segment: a system segment with flag references, owned by the overridden feature. Experiments' and phased rollouts' system segments must not match.
- The admin UI shows dependency overrides' value as inherited from the environment default.

title: Committing a segment change request leaves flag references stale
body:
`_publish_segments` copies the draft's rules into the live segment without re-indexing its `SegmentFlagReference` rows. Meanwhile, draft segments are indexed on creation, as `ChangeRequestSegmentSerializer` extends `SegmentSerializer`. After a commit, the live segment's references describe its old rules, and the draft keeps references of its own.

Cycle validation for drafts and commits is tracked in Flagsmith/flagsmith-private#296

### Steps to reproduce

1. With change requests enabled in the project, create a segment matching `$.flags["payments"].enabled` and override `checkout` with it.
2. Open a segment change request switching the condition to `$.flags["billing"].enabled`, and commit it.
3. List `checkout`'s dependencies: `payments` is listed, `billing` isn't.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Committing a segment change request re-indexes the live segment's flag references.
- [ ] Draft segments aren't indexed.
- [ ] Dependency lists, cycle validation and prerequisite deletion checks reflect the committed rules.

title: revalidateTag called while a Route Handler response is streaming is silently dropped
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/jmtorres/next-streamed-revalidate-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm start`
2. Load `/` twice. The timestamp comes from a `'use cache'` component tagged `demo`, so it stays the same.
3. `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/stream`. This route returns a streamed `Response` and calls `revalidateTag('demo', 'max')` about 100 ms later, before the stream closes.
4. Reload `/` as many times as you like. The timestamp never changes.
5. Control: `curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/direct`, which calls `revalidateTag('demo', 'max')` and then returns. Reload `/` twice and the timestamp changes.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: a `revalidateTag` that runs after the handler has returned its `Response`, while the body is still streaming, never takes effect. No error and no warning in dev or prod.

Expected: it's applied like any other revalidation in the request, or at least Next warns that the call was dropped.

What's happening: the route module applies pending revalidations exactly once, when the handler returns (`resolvePendingRevalidations()` → `executeRevalidates(workStore)` in `packages/next/src/server/route-modules/app-route/module.ts`, L486 at `13b59c9`). The app-route template reads `pendingWaitUntil` once right after (`build/templates/app-route.ts` ~L315). Anything queued later goes onto `workStore.pendingRevalidatedTags` and nothing ever reads it again.

How we hit it: we run Payload CMS with its MCP plugin. That plugin uses `mcp-handler`, whose Streamable HTTP transport returns the `text/event-stream` response before the tool runs. So every edit made through MCP fires the collection hooks, the hooks call `revalidateTag`, and the cached page never refreshes. Editing through the admin or REST works fine because those writes finish before the handler returns.

title: `@next/codemod agents-md`: docs `root` is relative to the cwd, not to the `--output` file (breaks monorepos)
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Stanzilla/next-agents-md-monorepo-repro

### To Reproduce

The reproduction is a pnpm workspace. `next@16.4.0` is a dependency of `apps/web` only, and `AGENTS.md` is at the repo root:

```
AGENTS.md
pnpm-workspace.yaml
apps/web/package.json   # depends on next@16.4.0
```

1. `pnpm install`
2. From the app: `cd apps/web && npx @next/codemod@16.4.0 agents-md --output ../../AGENTS.md`
3. Reset `AGENTS.md`, then from the repo root: `npx @next/codemod@16.4.0 agents-md --output AGENTS.md`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Step 2 (from the app).** The codemod logs `Using the docs bundled with Next.js 16.4.0 at ./node_modules/next/dist/docs` and writes `root: ./node_modules/next/dist/docs` into the root `AGENTS.md`. That path is relative to `apps/web`, the cwd. From the directory of `AGENTS.md` it does not exist, so every path in the index is broken.

**Step 3 (from the repo root).** `next` is not visible from the root, so the codemod downloads a second copy of the docs into `.next-docs` and adds it to `.gitignore`. The docs that ship with the installed `next` are not used.

Expected: the `root` is relative to the directory of the `--output` file. Step 2 would then write `root: ./apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/docs`.

The `agentRules` block that `next dev` writes already uses this convention. It tells agents to read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` "resolved from this file's directory" and notes that "in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root". `agentRules` writes `AGENTS.md` next to the app, so it does not help a monorepo that keeps one `AGENTS.md` at the root, which agents started at the root read. For that layout the codemod is the only tool, and it cannot produce a working root.

body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Stanzilla/next-turbopack-app-availability-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run dev` (`next dev --turbopack -p 3456`)
3. Open http://localhost:3456/

The repro is a Pages Router app with no `next.config`:

- `pages/_app.js` imports `lib/c-shared.js` and calls `import('../lib/app-dyn')`, which also imports `c-shared`.
- `pages/index.js` imports `a-page-only`, `b-boundary`, `c-shared`, `d-boundary`, `e-page` in that order, and calls `import('../lib/page-dyn')`, which imports `b-boundary` and `d-boundary`.

With the dev server running, `npm run check` lists which of these modules have a factory in the chunks that load for `/`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** The page server-renders, then crashes during hydration:

```
Module [project]/lib/a-page-only.js [client] (ecmascript) was instantiated because it was required from module [project]/pages/index.js [client] (ecmascript), but the module factory is not available.
```

No chunk that loads for `/` defines `a-page-only` or `b-boundary`. A clean `.next`, a hard reload and disabled browser cache give the same result. The message points at cache headers and service workers, but neither is involved.

title: Next 16.4: turbopackSharedRuntime inlines the bootstrap into the prerendered shell without a nonce, breaking hydration under a nonce CSP (cacheComponents)
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/stperic/next-shared-runtime-nonce-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repro, `npm install && npm run build && npm start`, open http://localhost:3000.
2. Next.js 16.4.0, App Router, Turbopack production build, `cacheComponents: true`.
3. A per-request nonce-based CSP from middleware/proxy, following the CSP guide: `script-src 'self' 'nonce-<random>'` (no `'unsafe-inline'`), set in `proxy.ts`.
4. The page has a prerendered shell plus a per-request Suspense hole.
5. The console shows two CSP violations and the counter button never responds.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the page never hydrates. Two inline scripts in the prerendered shell carry no `nonce` attribute, so the browser blocks them:

- `<script id="_R_">(globalThis["TURBOPACK"] || (globalThis["TURBOPACK"] = [])).push({"otherChunks":[...],"runtimeModuleIds":[...]})</script>`, the chunk-group bootstrap emitted when `experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` is on (the 16.4 default, `getTurbopackChunkGroupBootstrap` in `app-render`)
- `<script>requestAnimationFrame(function(){$RT=performance.now()});</script>`

Every other script in the same response (the per-request part) carries the nonce correctly. Because the bootstrap is blocked, the client runtime never starts: `window.next` is undefined and nothing is interactive.

On 16.2 the same app worked, because the bootstrap was an external `<script src>` that `'self'` allows. Setting `experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime: false` restores that behavior and hydration.

**Expected:** a nonce-based CSP keeps working with the default shared runtime. For example, inline bootstrap scripts in a prerendered shell could receive the request nonce when the shell is served or resumed, or the bootstrap could stay external when a nonce CSP is detected. At minimum, the CSP guide could document that `turbopackSharedRuntime` must be disabled under a nonce CSP with Cache Components / PPR.

title: Turbopack removes an IIFE in production builds when its inner callee is annotated /* @__PURE__ */
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/oenstrom/next-turbopack-pure-iife

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and install: `npm install`
2. Run `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:3000. The page shows:
   - `annotated IIFE: ran`
   - `plain IIFE: ran`
3. Run `npm run build && npm run start` (Turbopack) and open http://localhost:3000. The page shows:
   - `annotated IIFE: REMOVED`
   - `plain IIFE: ran`
4. For comparison, run `npx next build --webpack && npm run start`. Both lines show `ran`.

The relevant code in `app/page.tsx` is the shape esbuild emits for an IIFE with `keepNames`:

```js
;(/* @__PURE__ */ __name((function annotated() {
  annotatedCalls++
}), 'annotated'))()
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** The `/* @__PURE__ */` annotation applies only to the inner `__name(...)` call. The outer call, which invokes the returned function, is not annotated and has side effects, so it must be kept. `next dev` and `next build --webpack` both keep it.

**Current:** `next build` with Turbopack removes the whole IIFE. In the minified chunk, the effect becomes `l(["annotated IIFE: REMOVED", ...])`: the call is gone and the condition is constant-folded.

With `experimental.turbopackMinify: false`, the cause is visible. The parentheses around the annotated inner call are dropped during transformation, so the annotation ends up in front of the outer call:

```js
// input (@radix-ui/react-scroll-area@1.2.18, dist/index.mjs)
(/* @__PURE__ */ __name((function loop() { /* ... */ }), "loop"))();

// Turbopack output, minification disabled
/* @__PURE__ */ __name9(function loop() { /* ... */ }, "loop")();
```

After that, the minifier treats the outer call as pure and removes it.

title: Turbopack: chunk loader scans the whole DOM with querySelectorAll for every chunk (O(DOM × chunks) main-thread cost at boot)
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/ylcn91/next-turbopack-chunk-qsa-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction, then `npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm run build && npm start` (serves on port 3123).
2. In a second terminal run `npm run measure`. It loads `/?n=<elements>` at 500 / 2000 / 4000 / 8000 static elements next to 80 `next/dynamic` client widgets (one async chunk each), with CPU throttling 1x and 4x, and times only the runtime's chunk-presence probe.
3. Alternatively open `http://localhost:3123/?n=4000` in Chrome with CPU throttling 4x and record a performance profile: the boot / hydration tasks show self time in `querySelectorAll` called from `doLoadChunk` → `loadChunkCached` → `loadChunkByUrlWhole`, growing with `n`.

Result of `npm run measure` (Chromium, CPU 4x, 82 probe calls, median of 3):

| DOM elements | Time in the probe |
|---|---|
| 761 | 30.8 ms |
| 2,261 | 76.4 ms |
| 4,261 | 115.7 ms |
| 8,261 | 229.9 ms |

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src/browser/runtime/dom/runtime-backend-dom.ts` (canary, lines ~222 and ~255) checks whether a chunk tag already exists with

```ts
document.querySelectorAll(
  `script[src="${chunkUrl}"],script[src^="${chunkUrl}?"],script[src="${decodedChunkUrl}"],script[src^="${decodedChunkUrl}?"]`
)
```

(and the `link[rel=stylesheet][href…]` equivalent for CSS). Attribute and prefix (`^=`) selectors have no fast path, so each call walks the entire document. It runs once per chunk, so the cost is O(elements × chunks) on the main thread during boot/hydration.

On a production e-commerce listing page (~4,000 elements, 78 chunk probes) we measured:

| | CPU 4x |
|---|---|
| V8 CPU profile, self time in `querySelectorAll` under `doLoadChunk` | 97.5 ms |
| Instrumented `querySelectorAll` (78 calls, real production build) | 98–116 ms |

title: Prefetch loop: optimistic routing drops a parallel slot's catch-all param next to a static segment
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop

### To Reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/pablodecm/next-optimistic-routing-prefetch-loop and run `npm install`.
2. Run `npm run build && npm run start`.
3. Open `http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard` with the browser's Network panel open.
4. Do not click anything. Watch the RSC requests.

To count the requests without the Network panel, run `scripts/measure.sh http://localhost:3000/acme/dashboard out.har`.
It records the page for 10 seconds with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser) and prints the
prefetch requests per URL and segment.

The reproduction has this route structure, with `cacheComponents: true`:

```
app/
  layout.tsx
  [workspace]/
    layout.tsx                      renders {children} and {modal}
    @modal/
      default.tsx                   returns null
      [...catchAll]/page.tsx        returns null (clears the slot on soft navigation)
    dashboard/page.tsx              six <Link>s to /[workspace]/items/<n>/view
    items/[itemId]/view/page.tsx
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Expected:** each visible link is prefetched once (a `/_tree` request and its segments).

**Current:** after the first links are prefetched, one link sends the same segment prefetch over and over, about
65 times a second, for as long as the page is open. Every response is HTTP 200:
